title: The universal orbit–stabilizer divisibility law
content: The header frames this child against its parent `LagrangeFourSquaresOQ02`, which establishes the orbit–stabilizer identity contribution(t) = 384/|Stab(t)| case-by-case for six named type families (each with side hypotheses). This file proves the UNIVERSAL form contribution(t) ∣ 384 for every sorted representation type t of every n, with no case split and no hypotheses. Here 384 = |S₄ × (ℤ/2ℤ)⁴| = 24·16 is the order of the full symmetry group acting on ordered signed four-square representations.
mathContext: The parent file establishes the orbit–stabilizer identity $\mathrm{contribution}(t) = 384/|\mathrm{Stab}(t)|$ for six *named* type families (trivial, all-equal, three-equal, two-pair, two-equal, two-nonzero-distinct), each with side hypotheses. This file proves the UNIVERSAL form $\mathrm{contribution}(t) \mid 384$ for every sorted representation type $t$ of every $n$, with no case split. Here $384 = |S_4 \times (\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^4| = 24 \cdot 16$ is the order of the full symmetry group acting on ordered signed four-square representations.

title: RepType and its contribution data
content: The definitions reproduce the parent entry's `RepType` and contribution data verbatim so the file is self-contained. `RepType n` is a sorted 4-tuple (a₁ ≤ a₂ ≤ a₃ ≤ a₄) with a₁²+a₂²+a₃²+a₄² = n; `contribution = permutations · signFactor` counts the ordered signed representations it generates, where `permutations = 24 / ∏(count v)!` is the multinomial 4!/∏mᵢ! and `signFactor = 2^nonzeroCount` counts independent sign choices.
mathContext: `RepType n` is the sorted type $(a_1 \le a_2 \le a_3 \le a_4)$ with $a_1^2+a_2^2+a_3^2+a_4^2 = n$. Its `contribution = permutations · signFactor` counts the ordered signed representations it generates: `permutations = 24 / \prod_v (\mathrm{count}\,v)!` is the multinomial $4!/\prod_i m_i!$ (orderings of the multiset), and `signFactor = 2^{\mathrm{nonzeroCount}}` counts the independent sign choices. These mirror the parent entry's definitions verbatim so the divisibility law refers to exactly the same quantities.

title: The multinomial denominator divides 4! = 24
content: The combinatorial heart: for any four naturals the multinomial denominator ∏(count v)! divides 4! = 24 — the integrality of the multinomial coefficient for a 4-element multiset. The proof bridges the list-based definition to Mathlib's `Nat.prod_factorial_dvd_factorial_sum` using `List.prod_toFinset` (nodup list product = Finset product over toFinset) and the fact that the multiplicities sum to the list length 4.
mathContext: The combinatorial heart: for any four naturals the multinomial denominator $\prod_v (\mathrm{count}\,v)!$ divides $4! = 24$. This is the integrality of the multinomial coefficient specialised to a 4-element multiset. The proof bridges the list-based definition to Mathlib's Finset lemma `Nat.prod_factorial_dvd_factorial_sum` ($\prod_{i} (f\,i)! \mid (\sum_i f\,i)!$) using `List.prod_toFinset` (nodup list product = Finset product over toFinset) and `List.sum_map_count_dedup_eq_length` (the multiplicities sum to the list length 4).

title: Two independent factor divisibilities: 24 and 16
content: The contribution factors into two independently-bounded pieces: `signFactor = 2^nonzeroCount ∣ 16 = 2^4` (at most 4 nonzero entries, via `pow_dvd_pow`), the (ℤ/2ℤ)⁴ sign part; and `permutations = 24/D ∣ 24` (since the multinomial denominator D ∣ 24), the S₄ ordering part. Their product structure is exactly |S₄ × (ℤ/2ℤ)⁴| = 24·16 = 384.
mathContext: The two independent factor divisibilities: `signFactor = 2^{\mathrm{nonzeroCount}} \mid 16 = 2^4$ (since at most 4 entries are nonzero, via `pow_dvd_pow`), corresponding to the $(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^4$ sign part; and `permutations = 24/D \mid 24$ (since the multinomial denominator $D \mid 24$), corresponding to the $S_4$ ordering part. Their product structure is exactly $|S_4 \times (\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^4| = 24 \cdot 16 = 384$.

title: Main theorem: contribution ∣ 384 for every type
content: `contribution_dvd_384` multiplies `permutations ∣ 24` and `signFactor ∣ 16` via `mul_dvd_mul` to give contribution = permutations · signFactor ∣ 24·16 = 384 for EVERY type of EVERY n. Positivity (`contribution_pos`, ≥ 1) and the sharp upper bound (`contribution_le_384`, ≤ 384) follow immediately. Unlike the parent's per-family theorems, this requires no hypotheses on the entries.
mathContext: The main theorem `contribution_dvd_384`: multiplying `permutations ∣ 24` and `signFactor ∣ 16` via `mul_dvd_mul` gives $\mathrm{contribution} = \mathrm{permutations} \cdot \mathrm{signFactor} \mid 24 \cdot 16 = 384$ for EVERY type of EVERY $n$. Positivity (`contribution_pos`, $\ge 1$) and the sharp upper bound (`contribution_le_384`, $\le 384$) follow immediately. Unlike the parent's per-family theorems, this needs no hypotheses on the entries.

title: Stabilizer form: contribution = 384/|stab|
content: The orbit–stabilizer identity in native form. Defining stabOrder(t) := 384/contribution(t), the divisibility gives contribution · stabOrder = 384 (`Nat.mul_div_cancel'`), stabOrder ∣ 384, and the inverse contribution = 384/stabOrder (`Nat.div_div_self`). Thus the tabulated relation contribution = 384/|Stab| holds for all types simultaneously, with stabOrder playing the role of the stabilizer order.
mathContext: The orbit–stabilizer identity in native form. Defining $\mathrm{stabOrder}(t) := 384/\mathrm{contribution}(t)$, the divisibility gives $\mathrm{contribution} \cdot \mathrm{stabOrder} = 384$ (`Nat.mul_div_cancel'`), $\mathrm{stabOrder} \mid 384$, and the inverse $\mathrm{contribution} = 384/\mathrm{stabOrder}$ (`Nat.div_div_self`). Thus the tabulated relation $\mathrm{contribution} = 384/|\mathrm{Stab}|$ holds for all types simultaneously, with $\mathrm{stabOrder}$ playing the role of the stabilizer order.

title: Sharpness: 384 and 1 are both attained
content: The universal bound 384 is best possible and the unit 1 is attained. The fully asymmetric type (1,2,3,4) (all entries distinct and nonzero) has trivial stabilizer and contributes 24·16 = 384; the fully symmetric type (0,0,0,0) has the whole group of order 384 as stabilizer and contributes 1·1 = 1. Both witnesses are discharged by kernel `decide`, so — unlike the parent's `native_decide` computations — they add no `Lean.ofReduceBool` dependency.
